note: Forward predictions for 1.16 (Aegis of Dawn), authored by the pred-scout-coach agent on session compute (no API). Grounded in the digest's stated change numbers and the measured 1.15.4 ranked baseline (pred.gg general stats fetched 2026-08-07, version ids 157), the 8,105-match lane boards (meta.json 2026-08-07), the 2026-08-07 rank split (raw n/w cells; percentages computed as wins over games), and the 206,306-match feed head-to-heads. Forecasts, not measured post-patch results; no measured block yet. N3ON (Final Thread re-cast exploit fix) and Steel (Shield Slam blink exploit fix) are intentionally excluded as bugfix-only entries with no expected power movement. Scarlett is new: no baseline, no artifact, kit-only THEORY.

akeron.name: Akeron
akeron.why: Every scaling in the core loop is trimmed at once — Hellfire 18% -> 16% with a smaller homing radius, both Web Lash scalings 40% -> 35%, and the Consume bite 45% -> 40% — so the payoff his magical items buy shrinks while the base kit is untouched.
akeron.willChange: This walks back part of last patch's recovery: he reads 49.3% over 11,651 ranked games and 51.1% raw on the 685-game offlane board, with the Grux lane still against him (45% over 1,605 lanes). Expect a drift back below even, with the new Shrine skirmishes suiting his teamfight ult as the lone systemic consolation.

argus.name: Argus
changes: Mana Catalyst no longer restores mana on non-heroes (heroes 10% -> 12%)
argus.why: The sustain loop is the target: Mana Catalyst no longer restores mana on non-heroes, ending the camp-and-minion mana battery, while Particle Shredder loses top-end damage (13-41 -> 13-37), scaling 18% -> 16%, and gains half a second of cooldown.
argus.willChange: A tax on one of the strongest mid seats — 53.3% over 17,738 ranked mid games and 52.4% raw on the 1,452-game lane board — that trims his spam rather than his spikes. The Shrines' permanent ability haste partially refunds the cooldown nerf, so expect a modest pullback, not a fall; the AzureCore/Entropy line (57.6% over 784 games) stays the build.

countess.name: Countess
countess.why: Feast's payoff jumps at ranks two and three (135/185/235 -> 135/215/285) — up to 50 more finishing damage on the ability that decides her dives — plus a touch more health growth (130 -> 132) to survive them.
countess.willChange: A targeted lift for a hero underwater at 46.9% over 15,490 ranked games, and the map helps too: permanent ability haste from Shrines feeds a kit that lives on dash resets. The mid matchups stay hard (46.1% into The Fey over 2,099 lanes), so expect movement toward even rather than past it.

crunch.name: Crunch
changes: Falcon Crunch empowered damage 15% -> 20%, in-air cooldown +30% -> +25%
crunch.why: The mobility reaches further (Lunge Crunch additional distance 10% -> 15%) and the payoff punches harder (Falcon Crunch empowered damage 15% -> 20% with a smaller in-air cooldown penalty) — combo-loop quality rather than raw numbers.
crunch.willChange: From 48.5% over 15,274 ranked games this nudges rather than moves; the bigger tailwind is systemic, since jungle Crunch collects the ~35-40% camp-gold increase, and both Viper and Basilisk in his sim core now shred correctly after the bugfix wave. The Grux lane stays the wall (45% over 2,568 lanes).

dekker.name: Dekker
dekker.why: Physical power 60 -> 57 is the carry flatten landing on a support: it shaves her basic-attack poke between ability rotations and nothing else.
dekker.willChange: She holds the top support board seat — 53.4% raw over 1,961 games, 49.8% over 21,863 ranked overall — and her value is stuns, not basic attacks. Expect her to stay the number-one support, with the Shrine fights starting at 2:00 giving her lockdown even more to do.

drongo.name: Drongo
changes: Physical power 60 -> 57, growth 3.6 -> 3.8 (early flattened, scaling intact)
drongo.why: The standard flatten: physical power 60 -> 57 with growth 3.6 -> 3.8, so early trades soften while the late-game curve is repaid.
drongo.willChange: From 50.3% over 17,818 ranked carry games expect little net movement, and the new tower economy suits him — platings never expire, which rewards exactly the long-range chip he lands between fights. The Sparrow lane (48.1% over 9,906 lanes) should ease as she takes the harder nerf.

eden.name: Eden
eden.why: The hardest carry hit: physical power 53 -> 49 with growth to 4.0, the Focal Lens refund consolidated to 10% total, and Helios Core heat generation cut at the early ranks (20/35/50/65% -> 12.5/30/47.5/65%) — the early spike arrives later even though the top rank is untouched.
eden.willChange: The floor is the cost: she runs 49.8% over 15,781 ranked games but climbs with rank — 82 of 150 at Platinum in the fresh split (54.7%) — and the scaling ceiling, the Solaris/Vanquisher line at 62.5% over 342 games, survives because rank-four heat is unchanged. Expect weaker lanes, similar late games.

feng-mao.name: Feng Mao
feng-mao.why: The taxes hit tempo and pick damage together: health growth 135 -> 132, Hamstring's isolation damage down (25-69 -> 25-65) with bonus scaling 30% -> 25%, and the Earth Shatter reset window shortened 20s -> 14s — fewer double-ult picks per fight.
feng-mao.willChange: He is a top-three jungle board seat (52.9% raw over 915 games) but 48.9% over 14,922 ranked overall, and he already loses the mirrors that matter: 40.9% into Rampage over 1,969 lanes and 44.7% into Khaimera over 4,489. The camp-gold buff lifts every jungler equally, so the relative read is down — and Omen in his top field build loses refund too (25% -> 20%).

gadget.name: Gadget
changes: Tesla Dome now correctly shreds magical armor (bugfix)
gadget.why: Tesla Dome now correctly shreds magical armor — a silent bug meant the zone that defines her was hitting harder-armored targets than intended, so her measured record understates the 1.16 kit.
gadget.willChange: From 49.0% over 11,124 ranked mid games expect a genuine tick up with no play-style change, and the map compounds it: permanent tower platings reward a hero who sieges behind deployables. The Fey lane stays the check (46.7% over 3,516 lanes).

greystone.name: Greystone
changes: Make Way now correctly shreds magical armor (bugfix)
greystone.why: Make Way now correctly shreds magical armor — free damage from a bugfix — and it stacks with the same wave fixing Viper and Basilisk, the two items that open his sim core. Everything he was measured doing, he was doing with broken shred.
greystone.willChange: He was already the offlane: 53.5% over 23,652 ranked offlane games, 54.4% raw on the 2,333-game lane board, 55.3% into Terra over 2,192 lanes and 52.5% into Bayle over 5,476. A multi-layer shred restoration on the format's best offlaner is ban material; expect him to hold #1 with a higher ceiling, and the Overlord bruiser line (55.7% over 542 games) to stay the build.

grim-exe.name: GRIM.exe
grim-exe.why: A clean trim with no payback: physical power 56 -> 53 and no growth compensation, while Manta Scythe — sitting in his sim core — loses isolation damage (+10% -> +8%) in the same patch.
grim-exe.willChange: From 49.2% over 9,147 ranked carry games expect a small slide; the consolation is relative, since Sparrow (51.9% overall) takes a larger cut and the head-to-head (47.9% over 5,262 lanes) should tighten.

howitzer.name: Howitzer
howitzer.why: Physical power 57 -> 55 flattens the basic-attack poke between ability rotations; the ability kit is untouched.
howitzer.willChange: From 49.4% over 8,663 ranked mid games this barely registers, and the Shrines' permanent ability haste favors a hero who is all cooldowns — roughly a wash, with the Combustion skirmisher line (55.2% over 384 games) unchanged.

iggy-scorch.name: Iggy & Scorch
changes: Badlands Critter double-damage bugfix (damage down in practice)
iggy-scorch.why: The flatten (52 -> 49 with growth to 4.1) is cosmetic for a burn mage, but the Badlands Critter double-damage bugfix is a real damage cut in practice — this time the bug was working in his favor.
iggy-scorch.willChange: He is one of the patch's clearest overperformers — 54.2% over 7,114 ranked offlane games and 52.5% over 14,734 in mid — so this is a deliberate pull-down. The permanent-plating economy rewards his zone sieging in the other direction; expect him to fall from the top seats but stay comfortably playable.

ikra.name: Ikra
changes: Cascade reworked — no longer applies on-hit effects
ikra.why: The rework removes Cascade's on-hit application — the hybrid on-hit angle dies outright — alongside power 57 -> 55, a shorter Narcosis stun (1.2s -> 1.1s), a smaller Undertow refund, and Brine scaling 50% -> 45%.
ikra.willChange: She was already underwater at 46.5% over 15,517 ranked games, and the skill split is stark in the fresh cells: 124 of 277 at Silver (44.8%) against 42 of 74 in the Platinum midlane cell (56.8%). Unlike the last round of changes, these cuts land on the expert loop too — the stun and Brine are the combo — so expect both reads to drop.

maco.name: Maco
maco.why: Attack speed 120 -> 115 — a small trim to the on-hit poke, with nothing else touched.
maco.willChange: From 48.7% over 7,014 ranked support games expect little movement; the sustain squeeze around him (potions and the healing Eternals down again) matters more to a heal-and-harass support than the stat itself.

morigesh.name: Morigesh
changes: Spirit Shred now correctly shreds magical armor (bugfix buff)
morigesh.why: The flatten (52 -> 50, growth to 4.0) is the tax; the pay is Spirit Shred finally shredding magical armor as designed — meaning her measured record was earned with a broken shred.
morigesh.willChange: The 47.5% over 8,581 ranked games understates the 1.16 kit: every Mark rotation now softens the target properly. The hard lanes stay hard (43.3% into Renna over 1,751 lanes, 44.3% into The Fey over 1,770), so expect a climb toward even rather than a breakout — a quiet riser despite the mixed label.

murdock.name: Murdock
changes: Physical power 58 -> 55, growth 3.8 -> 4.0 (early flattened, scaling intact)
murdock.why: The flatten lands with compensation: physical power 58 -> 55 but growth 3.8 -> 4.0, so his early snipe-and-Buckshot pressure softens while the scaling repays it late.
murdock.willChange: He is the field's weakest premier carry — 46.7% over 20,837 ranked games, 46.4% into Sparrow over 11,261 lanes and 46.7% into Legion over 7,218 — but Sparrow takes a harder nerf (four power plus a passive cut), so those gaps should tighten even if his own number barely moves. The Crit Burst line (56.5% over 1,183 games) stays the build.

muriel.name: Muriel
muriel.why: Physical power 54 -> 52 with growth 3.4 -> 3.55 — the carry flatten grazing a support whose value is shields and the global ultimate, not basic attacks.
muriel.willChange: At 51.5% over 7,025 ranked games she is quietly healthy. Teleporters unlocking at game start slightly dilute her signature global-entrance advantage, while the constant Shrine skirmishes give the shields more to do; net expectation is flat.

narbash.name: Narbash
changes: Percussive Tear now correctly shreds magical armor (bugfix)
narbash.why: Percussive Tear now correctly shreds magical armor — a bugfix that pays the battle-Narbash pattern the 1.15.3 rework pushed him toward.
narbash.willChange: From 51.8% over 9,912 ranked support games expect a small tick up, concentrated in the Truesilver/Crystal Tear/Dynamo battle line already winning at 56.6% over 394 games.

phase.name: Phase
changes: Psychic Flare blink cooldown on hit 1s -> 2.5s
phase.why: Both changes tax the forward positioning that defines her: physical power 56 -> 54, and Psychic Flare's blink cooldown on hit rising 1s -> 2.5s — the aggressive blink weave now costs real recovery time every time it lands.
phase.willChange: She holds the #2 support board seat (52.0% raw over 1,443 games; 50.9% over 18,338 ranked) and the blink tax lands exactly on what makes her hard to punish. Expect a slide toward the support pack — the Dekker head-to-head (48.1% over 6,268 lanes) was already against her.

rampage.name: Rampage
changes: Tiny Titan size modifier -43% -> -33% (bigger hitbox on the shrink augment)
rampage.why: The lone change is a bigger hitbox on the shrink augment (Tiny Titan -43% -> -33%). Put plainly: the patch did not address the top winrate hero in the game — and the jungle economy rework pays him ~35-40% more camp gold on top.
rampage.willChange: He enters 1.16 at 55.5% over 16,616 ranked games (55.8% in jungle), 56.7% raw on the jungle board, 61.4% at Platinum (86 of 140) and 71.1% in the small Diamond+ cell (27 of 38), beating Khaimera 52.4% over 5,830 lanes and Feng Mao 59.1% over 1,969. Nothing here pushes back; expect him to stay #1, the Overlord/Rapture line (63.2% over 562 games) to stay dominant, and his ban rate (banned in 12.8% of 1.15.4 ranked matches while picked in 18.5% — the lobby lets him through more often than not) to climb.

revenant.name: Revenant
revenant.why: Physical power 55 -> 53 with no growth compensation — a straight trim to the early game, and Manta Scythe in his sim core is shaved too (+10% -> +8% isolation damage).
revenant.willChange: From 49.7% over 15,737 ranked carry games expect a small dip; the Sparrow lane (46.7% over 8,152 lanes) should ease as she is nerfed harder, and the Crit Burst line (55.1% over 1,029 games) is unchanged.

riktor.name: Riktor
riktor.why: Real damage on an all-in kit: physical power 62 -> 64, Zap O' 9-Chains damage per level 4 -> 5, and the Electrocute pulse modifier 50% -> 75% — the ult finally punishes what the hook starts. It lands in the patch where nearly every carry loses base power, so his all-ins connect against softer targets.
riktor.willChange: The fresh split says who this serves: he already wins at Platinum (83 of 154 overall, 53.9%; 72 of 124 as support, 58.1%) while Gold lobbies lose with him (160 of 363, 44.1%) and the support board tags him popular-but-losing at 48.7% over 1,301 games. More damage per hook shortens the follow-up the pick needs to pay off — expect the below-Platinum read to climb toward the Platinum one, and the sleeper jungle Riktor (53.3% raw over 214 games) to grow with the richer camps.

scarlett.name: Scarlett
changes: NEW HERO — melee offlane duelist running Energy instead of mana. Kit: Last Light (Energy passive), Ashen Vow, First Intent (dash), Minueta (multi-stab), Swan Song (restraining-stun ultimate with blade ignition). Three augments: Scarlet Dawn (mobility), Coup De Grace (dueling), Volcanic Slam (zone control).
scarlett.why: No baseline exists — the kit reads as a melee Energy-resource duelist: a dash (First Intent), a multi-stab (Minueta), and a restraining-stun ultimate (Swan Song), with three augment paths covering mobility, dueling, and zone control. Running Energy instead of mana sidesteps the ongoing mana-sustain squeeze entirely, and the reworked jungle buffs explicitly add Energy regen for her.
scarlett.willChange: The systemic winds favor her: the carry flatten hands lane bullies relative early power, and a restraining stun is a strong tool in the constant Shrine skirmishes. The measuring stick is Greystone (53.5% over 23,652 ranked offlane games) — that matchup will define her first weeks. Expect heavy pick experimentation and a wide skill spread; every read here is kit theory until measured data lands.

skylar.name: Skylar
skylar.why: Physical power 57 -> 54 with growth 2.4 -> 2.55 — early trades flattened, the missing-health execute scaling intact.
skylar.willChange: From 50.6% over 20,003 ranked carry games expect roughly flat: the whole carry class is being flattened together and her late execute still spikes. The Sparrow lane (48.7% over 8,668 lanes) should ease as the harder-nerfed side of it.

sparrow.name: Sparrow
sparrow.why: The heaviest carry flatten (physical power 61 -> 57, growth to 3.6) plus a passive cut (Relentless max-health damage 0.3% -> 0.25%) — and the Eternals pass trims Ferocity, the attack-speed minor most carries defaulted to, in the same patch. The best carry is nerfed from three directions at once.
sparrow.willChange: She enters as THE carry: 52.2% over 34,120 ranked carry games, #1 on the lane board (52.6% raw over 2,869), winning every premier head-to-head — 53.6% into Murdock over 11,261 lanes, 51.9% into Drongo over 9,906, 53.3% into Revenant over 8,152, 52.1% into TwinBlast over 6,315. Expect the largest carry fall of the patch and a genuinely open carry seat; the On-Hit line (56.2% over 1,173 games) stays her best expression, softened by the Ferocity trim.

terra.name: Terra
changes: Axe Retrieval also grants Highland Hurl +15% damage
terra.why: One clean buff: Axe Retrieval also grants Highland Hurl +15% damage, rewarding the catch-and-throw loop.
terra.willChange: A small kindness to a hero at 46.4% over 7,859 ranked games who loses both premier offlane matchups (44.7% into Greystone over 2,192 lanes, 47.2% into Grux over 2,257) — and the Greystone side of that just got a shred bugfix. Expect a nudge, not a recovery.

the-fey.name: The Fey
the-fey.why: Physical power 57 -> 55 with growth 3.2 -> 3.35 — the flatten grazing a mage whose damage is all abilities.
the-fey.willChange: The top mid board seat (52.9% raw over 1,588 games; 51.6% over 21,526 ranked mid) barely feels this, and permanent Shrine ability haste feeds her cooldown loop. Expect her to hold the seat, with the Combustion frontline line (55.6% over 1,073 games) unchanged.

twinblast.name: TwinBlast
twinblast.why: A trade, not a nerf: physical power 66 -> 63 (growth to 4.5) but Vaporize's on-hit rises 150% -> 170% and Vortex Grenade's cooldown drops — the payback flows into the ability loop. Separately, the Ashbringer cooldown-refund bugfix directly upgrades his top field build.
twinblast.willChange: From 47.5% over 13,637 ranked games he is a quiet riser candidate: the Solaris/Ashbringer/Imperator line (51.9% over 552 games) gets a free item fix, and the Legion lane (45.9% over 4,461 lanes) is where the gains are needed most. Expect movement toward even.

wraith.name: Wraith
wraith.why: Physical power 60 -> 57 with growth 3.0 -> 3.2 — a real early flatten on a poke pattern built around the sniper shot and basic attacks.
wraith.willChange: At 45.7% over 13,514 ranked games he enters with the weakest baseline of the flattened carries, and the mid matchups are already heavy (43% into The Fey over 2,374 lanes, 44.9% into Gideon over 1,817). Growth compensation pays too late for a hero losing lanes now; expect him to stay at the bottom.

zinx.name: Zinx
zinx.why: A multi-front nerf on a hero already below even: health 685 -> 670, physical power 50 -> 46, mana 340 -> 320, slower basic attacks (BAT 1.35 -> 1.4), the Terminal Treatment DoT bonus cut to +35%, and a much slower early Triage Protocol (24s at rank one, from a 17-4.25 curve) — while the patch's potion and healing-Eternal trims squeeze her sustain identity from the outside.
zinx.willChange: From 49.0% over 19,563 ranked games expect a clear fall, and it also taxes her best-kept secret: the offlane flex reading 51.6% over 3,780 ranked games and sleeper-tagged at 52.5% raw over 259 on the lane board. Hard to recommend in any seat until the next pass.

sectionMeta.tldr: 1.16 is a systems patch wearing a balance patch's clothes: Shrines start a permanent mini-objective war at 2:00 (+2 ability haste and 50 global gold per kill, stacking true damage to towers), teleporters open at game start, tower platings never expire, and jungle camps pay ~35-40% more gold. On top of that, a dozen-plus heroes lose 2-4 base physical power with growth compensation — early carry damage drops league-wide, handing relative power to lane bullies, all-in supports, and junglers. The loudest non-change is Rampage: the top winrate hero (55.5% over 16,616 ranked games) receives only a cosmetic-augment hitbox nerf, while the best carry (Sparrow, 51.9%) and the #2 support seat (Phase) take real cuts.
sectionMeta.heroes: The carry flatten defines the hero pass: Sparrow loses the most (four base power plus a Relentless cut) from the top of the carry board, Eden's early heat generation is nearly halved at rank one, Zinx is nerfed on five stats at once, and Iggy & Scorch (54.2% over 7,114 ranked offlane games) loses real damage through a bugfix. The buffs cluster around armor-shred repairs — Greystone, Gadget, Narbash, and Morigesh were all playing with silently broken shred, so their measured winrates understate their 1.16 kits; Greystone at 53.5% ranked offlane WITH the bug is the scariest case. Riktor's damage buff serves the all-in hook game that gets relatively stronger as every carry's early power drops.
sectionMeta.eternals: Four new Eternals arrive — Weald (execute projectiles), Rust (stacking armor shred that pairs naturally with the patch's shred-fix wave), Pilow (enemy damage-output debuff), and Satariel (takedown power at a health cost) — and Cauterize is deleted for Mechadrive's attack-weaving cooldown refunds. The sustain squeeze continues: Marrow is reworked to missing-health scaling, Immaculate drops to 12% (second consecutive trim), and the economy minors (The King, Aion, the new Roses cap) all pay less. Carry loadouts lose twice: Ferocity's attack speed per stack falls 1.25% -> 1% in the same patch as the base-power flatten.
sectionMeta.items: The story is the bugfix wave: Ruthless Broadsword, Viper, and Basilisk now actually shred physical armor and Magnify magical — and Viper opens most of the physical roster's sim cores, so sustained physical damage is silently stronger league-wide. Ashbringer's refund fix directly upgrades TwinBlast's top field build. Against that: potions are trimmed again (Refillable to 120-230, Divine to 150-260), Rebirth and Cursed Scroll are shaved, Manta Scythe and Omen lose a little, while Augmentation and Berserker's Axe gain power for bruisers.
sectionMeta.ranked: No ladder-system changes — the Daybreak v7 map, the Shrine war, and the carry flatten land in ranked immediately, with the Daybreak Invitational on the 15th-16th and Brawl returning as a separate queue. The fresh rank split says where to watch: Rampage is strongest exactly where games are decided (61.4% at Platinum on 86 of 140, 71.1% in the small Diamond+ cell), Riktor's buff should compress his Gold-tier losing record (44.1%) toward his Platinum one (53.9%), and the shred-bugfix winners will show first in the offlane, where Greystone already tops the board.

measured.source: pred.gg generalStatistic (RANKED): pre-patch baseline = pinned pre-patch files 1.15 + 1.15.3 + 1.15.4; patch window = version ids 158+159+160+161+162+163+164+165 (n>=200 both sides for deltas). Any unlisted hotfix released inside the window is measured as part of it.
